findings.issue: A memory slot written once with 0 at entry is re-read as unknown everywhere (P14): returns print as 'return memory from mem[288] len mem[288]', loop counters start at mem[288], call values are 'mem[288] wei', dead 'if mem[288]: revert' branches stay, and setWhiteList's selector (stored at _139 four lines earlier) prints as the function name 'mem[_139 len 4]' while its arguments are decoded.
findings.rule: mem[64] is set to 512 before any store at a non-constant address, and every later mem[64] is >= 512, so stores at mem[64] + c never reach [288, 320); fold mem[288] to 0, then fold the dead branches and resolve the selector word read back from the store at the same base.

findings.issue: The custom error with arguments prints as 32-byte words starting at the selector, so the account is split across two words; the non-via-IR contracts of this batch print the same error as 'revert with 0xe2517d3f, caller, <role>'.
findings.rule: When revert data has length 4 + 32k, print the 4-byte selector and then the k words starting at offset 4, regrouping the byte concatenation accordingly.

findings.issue: Address validations print in two odd forms; the shift in 'not mem[s len 12] << 160' is useless (and relies on 'not' binding looser than '<<').
findings.rule: not Mask(96, 160, x) and not (mem[s len 12] << 160) both mean x == address(x) (x < 2**96 makes the shift irrelevant); print 'require x == address(x)'.
